initial_message:
Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for that run. A follow-up rerun clears the printed backend as well.

Without the sibling edit, A→B→A can keep UI and backend aligned at `"input 2"`. Either interpretation of leftover keys should keep UI and printed state in sync; the #3512 unmount rule for an already-registered `persist_state=None` widget is that both sides reset in the same run.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: current develop / #17106
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright)

### Additional Information

Found during QA of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17106#issuecomment-5813147965.

Related:

- #3512 — unmount should reset both the widget UI and the Python value in the same run
- #17093 / #17106 — delayed first mount after a leftover pre-registration user key (out of scope here)
- #12880 — identity-by-key (out of scope)

initial_message:
[Bug] st.dataframe() / st.table() silently kill WebSocket when DataFrame has non-ASCII column names + emoji data (no traceback, session loss)

## Summary

`st.dataframe()` and `st.table()` silently close the WebSocket connection when the DataFrame contains **non-ASCII column names** (e.g. `ç`, `ê`, `/`) **combined with emoji in cell data**. No Python exception is raised, no error appears in the terminal — the browser simply reconnects with a brand-new session, wiping `st.session_state` entirely.

This is one of the hardest bugs to debug in Streamlit because it produces **zero tracebacks** and presents itself as an unrelated UX problem ("users keep getting logged out").

---

## Versions

| Package | Version |
|---|---|
| streamlit | 1.41.0 |
| pandas | 2.2.3 |
| Python | 3.11 |
| OS | Linux (Docker, python:3.11-slim) |

---

## Minimal Reproduction

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

# This persists fine
if "logged_in" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["logged_in"] = False

if not st.session_state["logged_in"]:
    if st.button("Login"):
        st.session_state["logged_in"] = True
        st.rerun()
    st.stop()

st.write("✅ Logged in — session_state alive")

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Serviço": ["Manutenção Website", "Hospedagem"],   # ← non-ASCII column name (cedilha)
    "Valor/mês": ["R$ 100,00", "R$ 200,00"],           # ← non-ASCII + slash in column name  
    "Status": ["🟢 Ativo", "🔴 Pausado"],              # ← emoji in cell data
})

st.dataframe(df)   # 💥 WebSocket dies here — no exception raised
st.write("This line never renders — session is already dead")
```

Run with Docker:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install streamlit==1.41.0 pandas==2.2.3
COPY app.py .
ENTRYPOINT ["streamlit", "run", "app.py", "--server.headless=true", "--server.fileWatcherType=none"]
```

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Build and run the container
2. Open `http://localhost:8501`
3. Click "Login" → session is alive (`session_state["logged_in"] = True`)
4. `st.dataframe(df)` renders (or tries to)
5. Browser reconnects → `session_state` is empty → "Login" button appears again

---

## Observed Behavior

- `st.dataframe(df)` call executes without raising any Python exception
- The line after `st.dataframe()` **never executes** (confirmed via `print()` to stdout)
- Browser-side: WebSocket closes and immediately reconnects with a fresh session
- `st.session_state` is wiped clean — any auth/navigation state is lost
- **Identical behavior with `st.table(df)`** — same root cause

### Diagnostic method that revealed the bug

Since no traceback is produced, the only way to isolate it was:

1. Store a UUID in `session_state` on first load: `st.session_state["sid"] = uuid4()`
2. Display it on every render: `st.caption(f"sid: {st.session_state['sid']}")`
3. Add `print()` statements throughout the render function (visible in Docker logs)
4. The `print()` output stopped exactly at the `st.dataframe()` call
5. The displayed `sid` changed to a new value on the next render → confirmed new WebSocket session

---

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The bug appears to occur during **Arrow/protobuf serialization** of the DataFrame when:
- Column names contain multi-byte UTF-8 characters (`ç` = U+00E7, `ê` = U+00EA, `/` combined with accented chars)
- AND cell data contains 4-byte Unicode emoji (`🟢` = U+1F7E2, `🔴` = U+1F534)

The serialization fails at the **protocol level** (WebSocket frame), not at the Python level. The exception is caught internally by Streamlit/PyArrow and manifests as a connection close rather than an error message.

The bug does **not** occur when:
- Column names are ASCII-only
- Cell data has no emoji
- `st.write(df.to_dict(orient="records"))` is used instead (routes through JSON, not Arrow)

---

## Workaround

Replace `st.dataframe()` / `st.table()` with a **GFM markdown table** rendered via `st.markdown()`:

```python
def _esc(v) -> str:
    """Escape pipe to prevent breaking markdown table structure."""
    return str(v).replace("|", "\\|")

lines = [
    "| Servico | Valor_mes | Status |",
    "|---|---|---|",
]
for _, row in df.iterrows():
    lines.append(f"| {_esc(row['Serviço'])} | {_esc(row['Valor/mês'])} | {row['Status']} |")

st.markdown("\n".join(lines))
```

This bypasses the Arrow serialization layer entirely.

---

## Expected Behavior

- `st.dataframe()` should either render the DataFrame correctly OR raise a visible Python exception / display an in-app error
- The WebSocket connection should **never** be closed silently due to a data rendering issue
- If Arrow serialization fails, Streamlit should fall back to a JSON/HTML representation rather than terminating the session

---

## Additional Notes

- `fileWatcherType = "none"` was confirmed active — rules out hot-reload as the cause
- The Docker container did **not** restart (verified via log message count)
- The bug is **100% reproducible** in the described environment
- Changing column names to ASCII-only (`Servico`, `Valor_mes`) likely resolves the Arrow schema issue

Would appreciate confirmation of the root cause and whether a fix is planned for 1.41.x or 1.42.0.

Deleting a widget's session_state key leaves the frontend showing the stale value (backend/frontend divergence for one rerun)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Deleting a keyed widget's entry from `st.session_state` (e.g. `del st.session_state["foo"]` inside a callback) does not reset the widget, but can lead to an inconsistency between frontend and backend.

The Python side returns the widget's *default* value for that run, but the frontend keeps displaying the old value, so backend and frontend disagree.

On the **next** rerun the backend silently re-adopts the stale frontend value, so the deletion is effectively undone.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

text = st.text_input("Foo", value="default", key="foo")

st.write("widget returned:", repr(text))

def populate():
    st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"

def delete():
    del st.session_state["foo"]

st.button("Populate", on_click=populate)
st.button("Delete", on_click=delete)
st.button("Noop")

```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app.
2. Click **Populate** (callback sets `st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"`). The text input now shows `hello` and `widget returned: 'hello'`.
3. Click **Delete** (callback runs `del st.session_state["foo"]`).
4. Observe the text input on screen vs. the `widget returned:` line.
5. Click **Noop** (any interaction that triggers a plain rerun) and observe again.

### Expected Behavior

The widget value in the frontent and backend should be consistent. After deleting a widget's key in session state, it should presumably fall back to its default value.

### Current Behavior

- After clicking Delete, the backend returns `widget returned: "default''` , but the frontend widget still displays `"hello"`.
- After the next rerun (step 5), the backend re-adopts the stale frontend value, and both show `"hello"`.

I'm trying to migrate our custom js widgets from v1 component api to the non-iframe v2 api.
It seems far more powerful, and seems like it'll cut boilerplate.
In our style, we have accumulated over the years a collection of js/client side running code, that doesn't particularly need/have an html or user-interfacing component.

I think I've noticed an issue, where values are getting returned from the js frontend (as seen by console.log msgs), but the streamlit backend logs see those msgs as dropped. I'm still getting the hang of the runtime behaviors of this new component api, to figure out how to update our v1 components, so I've been trying to test it. If this is not the expected or correct usage, I'm all ears, but I'm working my best from the online docs + repo src implementation. 

This is our current design / usage analysis of the v2 api:
- We declare/write a st.components.v2.component(...) object in a helper file, that will not be modified, with a unique name
- The js string includes all helper functions, and an `export default function(component: FrontendRendererArgs)`
- This default function is the per-widget-instantiation, and only run once (see below)
- It sets up callbacks or such on html elements
- If the component is called with a `key`, then all setTriggerValue and setStateValue items populate session_state
- Without an explicit `key`, setTriggerValue won't populate session_state, but the rest of the python arguments (data) are used to calculate a unique frontend key
- No two component instances therefore can have the exact same args (data)
- If the args to the component don't change, the widget object stays created, and is not re-instantiated
- If the rest of the args (data) to the component change, without a `key`, the old widget is discarded, and a new component is instantiated

Our goal is to have high-level code that uses caching & post processing of raw lower-level data call these low-level components as needed. But if the components are called, I expect them to behave consistently. 

In this particular example, the js component does (for example!!!) a failproof cookies query on instantiation and returns it via setTriggerValue.
```js
export default function (component){  component.setTriggerValue("get_cookies", document.cookie); }
```
We wrap that `st_comp_get_cookies: st.components.v2.component` in a helper function.
```python
def get_raw_cookies():
    obj = st_comp_get_cookies(data={"_": unique_line_time()})
```
If we feed `data` a value that's unique to the line (line traceback stack), the multiple calls of the widget will be unique even if fed the same other args. It would create a new component when there's a new/unique call (args or location), otherwise only instantiated once.
If we feed `data` a value that's unique in time, then every call is a new widget instance, and the js default function runs each time.

In the v1 api, when the app first loaded, the components wouldn't always respond right away. So I'd check if the returned value was empty or not.
```python
# get_raw_cookies()
if not isisntance(obj, dict) or "get_cookies" not in obj:
    # Very first run, component mightn't be ready
    time.sleep(initial_setup_sleep)
    st.rerun()
print(f"{obj["get_cookies"]=}")
```

Given the above files, with more logging added, I noticed a very strange behavior. (This is just a heavily reduced version of our real prod code; and I only chose documents.cookies because it _can't fail_).
In the browser console, everytime the page reloaded (hard reload F5, or soft rerun from some other input), the console logged the new widget instance, the cookie fetch, and that succeeded.
But in the python logs, sometimes it worked, sometimes it did not. 
With the "rerun if fail" check, if this was the only indeterminite execution, it'd work quickly enough, and then the rest of the code would execute.
But with multiple components doing this, it suddenly became impossible for both to work at the same time.
```python
get_raw_cookies() # Sometimes reruns, ok
get_raw_cookies() # Always reruns, when the above finally works
st.header("This never runs")
assert False
```

Sorry if this was rather long winded, but I'm either uncertain I'm understanding the runtime behaviors correctly, trying not to misrepresent our goals, possibly oblivious to a better v2 design, or just unaware of what to reasonably expect from this as for behavior.

initial_message:
AppTest: synchronize query parameters when interacting with query-bound widgets

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Please make AppTest's widget interaction API synchronize query parameters for widgets using `bind="query-params"`. Currently, `.set_value(...).run()` changes the widget value but leaves both `at.query_params` and the app's `st.query_params` unchanged, so tests observe a different state from the browser.

### Why?

Native query-param binding lets apps replace manual URL callbacks. After that change, AppTest tests that verify shareable filters or inspect `st.query_params` can no longer reproduce the state reached by the same user interaction in the browser. Each test must manually mirror the binding's serialization into `at.query_params`.

The following self-contained example demonstrates the gap on Streamlit 1.65.0; it also occurs on 1.64.0:

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

st.selectbox("FC", ["A", "B"], key="fc", bind="query-params")
st.session_state["seen_query"] = dict(st.query_params)
""").run()

at.selectbox[0].set_value("B").run()
assert not at.exception
print("Widget:", at.selectbox[0].value)
print("AppTest query params:", at.query_params)
print("App query params:", at.session_state["seen_query"])
```

Save as `repro_query_binding.py` and run `python repro_query_binding.py` with `streamlit==1.65.0` installed. No pytest or app-specific dependencies are required.

Observed:

```text
Widget: B
AppTest query params: {}
App query params: {}
```

In a browser, selecting B in the app string above updates the URL to `?fc=B` and the script sees `{"fc": "B"}`. The same AppTest gap occurs with `st.text_input(..., key="fc", bind="query-params")` and `at.text_input[0].set_value("B").run()`.

### How?

Use the existing interaction API to model the bound query-param update when a widget commits a value. For the example above, the desired result after `.set_value("B").run()` is:

```text
Widget: B
AppTest query params: {'fc': 'B'}
App query params: {'fc': 'B'}
```

The interaction should send a coherent widget-state/query-string pair using the widget's binding semantics, including serialization and clearing of the bound parameter. Unrelated query parameters should remain intact. This can be supported in the existing browserless AppTest API; a new browser runner is not requested.

A current workaround is to set the query params manually in the test before the run:

```python
at.selectbox[0].set_value("B")
at.query_params["fc"] = "B"
at.run()
assert at.session_state["seen_query"]["fc"] == "B"
```

This works, but the test must duplicate application binding logic. Keeping explicit `on_change` callbacks that write `st.query_params` also works, at the cost of retaining the application glue that native binding could replace.

### Additional Context

#### Environment and controls

- Streamlit: 1.65.0, also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python: 3.14.8.
- OS: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest example. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS and confirmed correct binding on both versions.
- The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes; no installed source was modified.
- Initial URL values correctly seed a bound widget in AppTest.
- Programmatically changing `st.session_state["fc"]` before rendering the bound widget correctly updates query params.
- Manual URL-writing callbacks work in AppTest.

#### Related work checked

- [#16906](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16906) requests a first-party browser-testing API. This request targets bound-widget query serialization during existing AppTest interactions.
- [PR #17191](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17191), included in 1.65.0, fixes single-value/list representation in `at.query_params`. The example still returns an empty dict after that fix.
- [PR #16998](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/16998) fixes browser back/forward restoration. This example changes a widget through AppTest and performs no history navigation.

I did not find an existing issue requesting this specific AppTest behavior. I am using the feature-request form because this extends the test simulation; the runtime binding itself works in the tested browser examples.

[LocalScriptRunner.run](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/local_script_runner.py#L170) constructs the query string from the query params passed by AppTest. The current widget interaction path does not generate the corresponding query-param update that a browser would send.

initial_message:
`setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`

### Summary

When a Components V2 component calls `setTriggerValue` during mount (inside the default function, rather than from a user event handler), values are silently lost if the component remounts because its `data` changed — even when an explicit `key` is passed, which keeps the element id stable.

Measured roughly a quarter loss: **5 of 21 values sent were never received by Python at all.** They are not late — a scan of the entire session log shows they never arrive in any subsequent run.

This is split out of #14710, where it surfaced during investigation. It is distinct from the two by-design mechanisms discussed there (`data` participating in element identity for unkeyed components, and trigger values resetting after each run).

**Update — measured root cause.** A frontend race in `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive`: it destroys the synthetic trigger-aggregator widget state while that state is still awaiting its batched flush, so the app reruns with no trigger at all. Not a backend discard. Measured on a production build with the repro below: 10/85 values lost unpatched vs 0/85 patched, and with instrumentation, 14/14 losses correlated exactly with the destroying call. Mechanism and open question under Additional Information.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

comp = st.components.v2.component(
    "repro.mount_trigger",
    js="""
    export default function (component) {
        const v = "val" + component.data.nonce;
        console.log("SEND " + v);
        component.setTriggerValue("v", v);
    }
    """,
)

if "clicks" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.clicks = 0
if st.button("bump"):
    st.session_state.clicks += 1

nonce = f"c{st.session_state.clicks}"
result = comp(data={"nonce": nonce}, key="stable_key")

received = result.get("v")
st.write(f"data nonce {nonce} -> received {received!r}")
print(f"nonce={nonce} received={received!r}", flush=True)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and open the browser console.
2. Click **bump** ~20 times, letting the app settle between clicks. Each click changes `data`, so the component remounts and sends one value.
3. Compare the `SEND val…` lines in the console against the `received=…` lines in the terminal.
4. Roughly one in four sent values never appears on the Python side.

### Expected Behavior

Every value the mounted component sends is readable on the following script run. The explicit `key` makes the element id stable, so a changing `data` payload should not affect delivery.

### Current Behavior

About 25% of values are never delivered. Verified as lost rather than late by scanning the full backend log after all clicks — 0 arrived in a later run.

The element id was logged each run and confirmed identical throughout (`$$ID-b4c118c7288cf7d656c205e58a384db6-stable_key`), so this is not the identity churn that affects unkeyed components.

Three controls on the same harness came out clean. They do not isolate the bug to trigger-on-mount — see Additional Information — but they do narrow which write path is affected:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| `setStateValue` on mount, same conditions | 21/21 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, stable `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, churning `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| **`setTriggerValue` on mount, churning `data`** | **5 of 21 lost** |

### Additional Information

**Mechanism.** `setTriggerValue` writes to a synthetic aggregator widget id (`makeTriggerAggregatorId` → `$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<componentId>__events`) and the flush is deferred to a `setTimeout(…, 0)` macrotask. `App.removeInactiveWidgetState()` runs from the `ScriptFinished` → `clearStaleNodes` setState callback and deletes every widget state whose id is not an active *element* id — the aggregator id never is, because it isn't part of the element tree. When that lands before the flush, the trigger is deleted but the rerun is still sent (`sendUpdateWidgetsMessage` uses unfiltered `createWidgetStatesMsg()`), so the script reruns with no trigger.

Mount-time triggers are the most exposed path: the component's `default function` runs behind `await loadAndRunModule(...)` (dynamic `import()` of a blob URL), so it executes a macrotask or more after the commit that mounted it. This also explains the control table — `setStateValue` is immune because it writes the component's real element id, and the event-handler controls passed because letting the app settle means `removeInactive` has already run.

**The `_pending_resets` theory is ruled out.** It is only populated by `mark_page_switch_drops`, which runs on page transitions and skips widgets whose recorded page is the current page, so a single-page app never populates it. (For the record, the original hypothesis was that `_pending_resets` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py` discarded a frontend-resent value on re-registration, which would have made this by design.)

**Related blind spot.** The same synthetic id is invisible to other active-id filters, not just this one: `App.tsx` `onPageChange` sends `getActiveWidgetStates(activeWidgetIds)`, which would likewise drop a pending aggregator. Reaching it would require a trigger and a page navigation in the same macrotask, and dropping a trigger while navigating away is defensible, so no change is planned there. Recorded as an observation only.

**Scope of what was tested.** Measured against this repro on one machine, 235 trials total. It establishes this race as the cause of the loss seen here; it does not rule out other trigger-loss paths. The same race also appears to explain the recurring `bidi_components/basics_test.py::test_trigger_interactions` CI flake — the failure signature (counts unchanged plus `Result` reset to `None`) is what a trigger-less rerun produces — but that link is inferred from the signature, not directly observed. Two prior automated PRs (#14542, #14843) misattributed that flake to a slow iframe round-trip and raised timeouts.

**Open question for Components V2** (replacing the original question here, which is now answered — the drop is a race, not intentional): should `setTriggerValue` during mount be a supported pattern at all? Fixing the race makes it reliable, but it fires on every remount, so churning `data` produces one trigger per remount. That is a semantics decision independent of this bug, and it determines whether this issue closes as fixed or splits into a fix plus a documentation/warning change.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (released wheel, production frontend build)
- Python version: 3.11 · macOS · Chromium
- The ~25% figure is one 21-trial sample on a single machine; treat it as "roughly a quarter" rather than a precise rate.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.

### Summary

AppTest loses a conditional text input's value when it is hidden and shown again with `persist_state="page"`, although the test never switches pages. The same sequence retains the value in a browser, and `persist_state="session"` works in AppTest.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

if st.toggle("Show", key="show"):
    st.text_input("SKU", key="sku", persist_state="page")
""").run()

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
at.text_input[0].set_value("SKU-42").run()
at.toggle[0].set_value(False).run()
print("While hidden:", repr(at.session_state["sku"]))
assert at.session_state["sku"] == "SKU-42"

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
print("After showing again:", repr(at.text_input[0].value))
assert not at.exception
assert at.text_input[0].value == "SKU-42"  # Fails: actual value is "".
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Streamlit 1.65.0 in a normal Python environment: `pip install streamlit==1.65.0`.
2. Save the example as `repro_page_persistence.py` and run `python repro_page_persistence.py`. Pytest is not required.
3. Observe that the hidden value is still `SKU-42`, but the final input value is empty and the final assertion fails.
4. Change `persist_state="page"` to `persist_state="session"` and run again. The value remains `SKU-42` and the assertion passes.
5. For a browser comparison, save only the app string as `app.py`, run `streamlit run app.py`, enable Show, enter `SKU-42` and press Enter, then disable and re-enable Show. The browser retains the input value.

### Expected Behavior

Page-scoped persistence should keep the value through the hide/show sequence in AppTest because the test remains on the same page. It should return `SKU-42` after the input is shown again, matching the browser.

### Current Behavior

Reproduced on both Streamlit 1.64.0 and 1.65.0:

```text
While hidden: 'SKU-42'
After showing again: ''
AssertionError
```

There are no application exceptions in `at.exception`; the failure is the final test assertion. A browser comparison on both versions retains `SKU-42`. AppTest's `persist_state="session"` control also retains it; the default `persist_state=None` control resets it as expected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

A previously working version has not been established. The versions tested are 1.64.0 and 1.65.0.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0; also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python version: 3.14.8.
- Operating System: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest reproduction. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS.
- Package integrity: The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes. No installed Streamlit source was modified.

### Additional Information

#### Related issues checked

- [#17119](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17119) concerns the remount of a `persist_state=None` widget and a backend/frontend mismatch. This reproduction uses explicit page persistence and works in a browser.
- [#17093](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17093) concerns a delayed first mount after a session-state value was set. Here, the widget was mounted, edited, hidden, and remounted.
- [#16611](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16611) concerns `AppTest.switch_page()` with a custom `url_path`. This example has no page switch or custom URL path.
- [#9128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9128) and [#12566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12566) report KeyErrors with changing widget trees. This example has no script exception and loses a page-persistent value.

I did not find an existing issue with this same reproduction.

#### Possible cause

AppTest creates a fresh PagesManager for each run. Its current page hash initially equals `""`. ScriptRunner interprets the mismatch with the target page hash as a page change and performs cleanup before resetting the context, so page-scoped persistence can be evaluated against the empty current hash.

Source links are pinned to the inspected develop commit `ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e`:

- [AppTest creates PagesManager](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py#L506).
- [PagesManager initializes an empty current page hash](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/pages_manager.py#L50).
- [ScriptRunner performs page-change cleanup before context reset](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py#L660).

In a separate single-page diagnostic on both released versions, seeding the reconstructed runner's current page hash with the main page hash before cleanup makes this reproduction pass. It also prevents a keyed stateful tab from resetting after a child-widget interaction in AppTest. This diagnostic is evidence about the cleanup path; a complete fix must still handle real page switches correctly. The develop source was inspected, not executed.

st.cache_data shares cache across st.Page pages for same-named functions with different source code

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.cache_data functions with the same name but different source code in different page files (loaded via st.navigation + st.Page) share the same cache. This is because st.Page executes all pages via exec() with
  __module__ == "__main__", and inspect.getsource() fails in that context. The fallback to func.__code__.co_code (bytecode) does not include string constants, so functions with identical structure but different inline strings (e.g., different SQL queries) produce the same cache key.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# main.py
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(page_title="Cache Bug Demo", layout="wide")
pg = st.navigation(
    {
        "Page A": [st.Page("page_a.py", title="Page A")],
        "Page B": [st.Page("page_b.py", title="Page B")],
    }
)
pg.run()
# page_a.py
import streamlit as st


[USER].cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_a", "columns": ["col_a1", "col_a2"]}


data = load_data()
st.write("Page A data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_a, Got:", data["source"])
# page_b.py
import streamlit as st


[USER].cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_b", "columns": ["col_b1", "col_b2"]}


data = load_data()
st.write("Page B data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_b, Got:", data["source"])
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create the three files above (main.py, page_a.py, page_b.py)
2. Run streamlit run main.py
3. Open Page A — displays source: page_a (correct)
4. Navigate to Page B — displays source: page_a (wrong, should be page_b)
5. Clear cache and open Page B first — displays source: page_b (correct)
6. Navigate to Page A — displays source: page_b (wrong, should be page_a)

### Expected Behavior

Each page's load_data() should have an independent cache, since they are defined in different files with different source code. Navigating between pages should return each page's own data.

### Current Behavior

Whichever page is loaded first caches its result under the function key. When the other page calls its own load_data(), the cached result from the first page is returned, because both functions produce the same cache key.

Root cause: In streamlit/navigation/page.py, st.Page.run() executes page scripts as:

module = types.ModuleType("__main__")
exec(code, module.__dict__)

This means func.__module__ is "__main__" for all pages. When inspect.getsource() fails in this exec() context, _make_function_key falls back to func.__code__.co_code, which does not include string constants — so
  structurally identical functions with different inline values produce the same key.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Python version: 3.14.3
- Operating System: macOS Tahoe Docker Desktop `FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.14-trixie-slim`

### Additional Information

Related issue: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11157 (cache_data cannot detect difference in values of free variables). That issue covers a similar problem with closure variables, but the st.Page + exec() scenario is a distinct trigger.

Workaround: Give cached functions unique names per page (e.g., page_a_load_data, page_b_load_data).

    if "repro_model" in sys.modules:

initial_message:
Add an option to fully disable sidebar rendering until authentication or page load is complete

Currently, Streamlit always renders the sidebar and multipage navigation menu before any backend logic runs.
This causes a brief flash (“flicker”) of the sidebar, even when developers try to hide it using CSS, st.set_page_config(initial_sidebar_state="collapsed"), or st.stop() during login checks.

Problem

When implementing authentication or loading processes (e.g., validating user credentials via an API), Streamlit renders the sidebar before the authentication state is known.
This behavior creates two key issues:

Security concern:
Unauthenticated users can briefly see and click sidebar navigation links before st.stop() halts the script, allowing them to access or attempt to load protected pages.
Even if no data is exposed, it creates a visible loophole and inconsistent behavior.

UX inconsistency:
The sidebar “flashes” for a fraction of a second during app load, even when the developer intends to display only a centered login screen or full-screen loading animation.
This leads to a jarring visual experience and makes professional deployments look less polished.

Why this matters

Many enterprise and production Streamlit apps use custom login systems, SSO integrations, or data validation APIs before showing any content.

In these cases, developers need full control over what renders before authentication completes.

There’s currently no reliable way to prevent the sidebar or multipage navigation from being rendered briefly.


Proposed solution

Add a configuration flag such as:
st.set_page_config(show_sidebar_on_load=False)
